title: Meet True and False
idea: Python has two special values for yes/no facts: True and False. They are called booleans. This lesson shows them with visible output.

exercises.prompt: Python has two special words for yes and no. What are they?
exercises.explanation: In Python the two yes/no values are True and False. These are called booleans.

exercises.prompt: In Python, the value True must start with a capital T.
exercises.explanation: Yes. Python is picky: it must be True (capital T) and False (capital F). Lowercase 'true' is not the same.
print(True) shows the boolean value exactly: True.
print(False) shows False. True and False are the only two boolean values.

exercises.prompt: Which of these is written correctly for Python?
exercises.explanation: Only 'True' with a capital T is the real boolean. The others are typos or wrong capitalization.

exercises.prompt:
Fill in the yes/no value that means 'no':

print(____)   # shows: False
exercises.explanation: False is the boolean that means 'no'. Remember the capital F.

exercises.prompt: True and False are the only two boolean values in Python.
exercises.explanation: Correct - a boolean is always either True or False. There is no third option.

exercises.prompt: Arrange the tokens to print the yes/no value True.
exercises.explanation: print(True) prints the boolean True. You just used a brand-new kind of value!

exercises.prompt: A friend writes print(true) and gets an error. Why?
options: 'true' is lowercase; Python needs True with a capital T
True is not a real value
exercises.explanation: Python only knows True and False with capital letters. Lowercase 'true' looks like an undefined name, so it errors.

exercises.prompt: What word do we use for these two special values, True and False?
exercises.explanation: True and False are called booleans - the data type for yes/no facts.
